name: NA62 refined measurement of the K+ -> pi+ nu nubar branching ratio (2026 update)
title: NA62 Collaboration refines measurement of rare particle decay

date.note: This is a CERN news article about a conference presentation (2026 La Thuile conference); no arXiv/journal identifier for this specific update was found by a source fetched this session.

claim.quote: The NA62 Collaboration refines the measurement of an extremely rare process

summary.plain: An update, presented at a March 2026 conference, that sharpens NA62's measurement of the rare kaon decay using more data, including runs from 2023 and 2024, cutting the uncertainty on the earlier 2025 observation.
summary.technical: Refined B(K+ -> pi+ nu nubar) = (9.6+1.9-1.8) x 10^-11, combining all NA62 data recorded since the experiment began (including newly added 2023-2024 data), with about 40% smaller uncertainty than the previously published (2025) result; presented at the 2026 La Thuile conference.

why_it_matters: Tracks NA62's continuing improvement in precision on one of the cleanest Standard Model tests in kaon physics as more data (2023-2024) is added beyond the 2025 observation paper.

key_value_text.value: B(K+ -> pi+ nu nubar) = (9.6+1.9-1.8) x 10^-11, combining data taken since the experiment began plus newly incorporated 2023-2024 data, ~40% smaller uncertainty than the previous (2025) result

significance.locator: home.cern news article, 4 March 2026 (no sigma value restated for this update)
significance.note: The news article references the earlier 2024/2025 discovery-level (5 sigma) result but does not itself restate a sigma value for this refined 2026 measurement; left null rather than assumed unchanged.

notes: Bonus (non-mandatory) third NA62 result, included because a source was available; sourced only to a CERN news article about a conference talk, not a peer-reviewed publication -- flagged accordingly in confidence/notes throughout.
